nagoya_koshitsu_kaiseki_hosatei.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Courses and compositions transcribed from the shop's own site (hosa.nagoya), snapshot dated 2026/07; the kaiseki line-up is seasonal and the version published at this check is the autumn one.

items.section: 会席料理 / Kaiseki courses (private room, reservation required)
items.note: The house course and the reason to book the private room: nine small courses in the classic kaiseki running order — appetiser, clear soup, a composed plate, sashimi, grilled, fried, hotpot, rice, sweet. Reserve by 17:00 two days ahead; you cannot request a specific room. The tempura course and the soy-based seasonings put wheat through it, and dashi runs through the whole meal.

items.en: "Kinjō" kaiseki course — eight courses, weekdays only
items.section: 会席料理 / Kaiseki courses (private room, reservation required)
items.note: The shorter weekday-only course, named for Nagoya Castle (金城 is its old poetic name). Same shape as the ¥5,500 course but drops the clear soup and simplifies the composed plate — the cheapest way into the private rooms. Wheat via the tempura and the soy seasonings.

items.ja: 一色産ひつまぶし和膳
items.en: Hitsumabushi set with eel from Isshiki
items.section: 会席料理 / Kaiseki courses (private room, reservation required)
items.note: A four-part set built around hitsumabushi — grilled eel from Isshiki in Aichi, the country's biggest eel-farming town, chopped over rice in a wooden tub. Eat it in three stages: quarter the rice, take the first plain, the second with the yakumi (spring onion, wasabi, nori), the third with dashi poured over as ochazuke, then the fourth whichever way you liked best. The eel tare is wheat soy sauce.

items.section: 会席料理 / Kaiseki courses (private room, reservation required)
items.note: Two price points of a chef's-choice course, above the two fixed ones — this is also the tier used for evening banquets (from ten people, ¥8,800 each, 17:00–21:00). Everything is bought that morning from the market, so the content is decided on the day.

items.ja: 先附：鯛の焼霜　舞茸　蕃茄　加減酢ジュレかけ
items.romaji: Sakizuke: Tai no Yakishimo, Maitake, Banka, Kagenzu Jure-gake
items.en: Opener: seared sea bream, maitake mushroom, tomato, seasoned-vinegar jelly
items.section: 会席「蓬左」の献立 / Inside the ¥5,500 course
items.note: 先附 (sakizuke) is the first tiny plate of a kaiseki, the equivalent of an amuse. 焼霜 means the fish is blowtorched on the skin side only and chilled, so the skin is smoky and the flesh raw. 蕃茄 is an old written form of tomato. The 加減酢 dressing usually contains dashi and sometimes soy, so ask.

items.ja: 御椀：梭子魚の菊花沢煮仕立て
items.en: Clear soup: barracuda with chrysanthemum petals, sawani style
items.section: 会席「蓬左」の献立 / Inside the ¥5,500 course
items.note: The 御椀 is the lacquer bowl of clear dashi soup that is the technical showpiece of a kaiseki — lift the lid and smell it before drinking. 梭子魚 is barracuda; 沢煮 is a light peppery broth with fine-cut vegetables. Bonito dashi rules it out for vegans; the seasoning may include a splash of light soy.

items.ja: 口取：月見豆腐　鹿児島和牛ステーキ　秋野菜炊合わせ
items.romaji: Kuchitori: Tsukimi-dōfu, Kagoshima Wagyū Sutēki, Akiyasai Takiawase
items.en: Composed plate: "moon-viewing" tofu, Kagoshima wagyu steak, simmered autumn vegetables
items.section: 会席「蓬左」の献立 / Inside the ¥5,500 course
items.note: 口取 is the plate of several small things served together. 月見豆腐 is tofu topped with an egg yolk standing in for the harvest moon; 炊合わせ means each vegetable is simmered separately in its own dashi so it keeps its own colour and flavour, then arranged together. The steak sauce is wheat soy.

items.section: 会席「蓬左」の献立 / Inside the ¥5,500 course
items.note: 造り is the sashimi course; 活魚 means the fish was alive in the tank, so what arrives depends on the morning market. The fish itself is clean — it is the soy sauce beside it that is wheat, so ask for tamari if you need it.

items.ja: 焼物：秋味と占地　杉板焼き
items.en: Grilled course: autumn salmon and shimeji mushrooms cooked on a cedar plank
items.section: 会席「蓬左」の献立 / Inside the ¥5,500 course
items.note: 秋味 is the trade name for autumn-run chum salmon; 占地 is shimeji. 杉板焼き cooks it on a sheet of cedar over the fire so the wood resin perfumes the fish — you will smell it before it lands. Whether the glaze contains soy or miso is the thing to ask.

items.ja: 揚物：穴子と二種の野菜　天麩羅
items.romaji: Agemono: Anago to Nishu no Yasai Tempura
items.en: Fried course: conger eel and two vegetables, tempura
items.section: 会席「蓬左」の献立 / Inside the ¥5,500 course
items.note: 穴子 is saltwater conger eel — milder and fluffier than the freshwater unagi in hitsumabushi, and superb as tempura. This is the unambiguous wheat course: tempura batter is wheat flour, and the tentsuyu dipping broth is dashi plus soy.

items.ja: 鍋物：名古屋コーチン　玉子とじ鍋
items.en: Hotpot: Nagoya Cochin chicken bound with egg
items.section: 会席「蓬左」の献立 / Inside the ¥5,500 course
items.note: 名古屋コーチン is Aichi's own heritage chicken breed — firmer and far more flavourful than supermarket bird, and one of the genuinely local things on this menu. 玉子とじ means beaten egg is poured over at the last moment and left barely set. The simmering liquid is dashi, soy and mirin.

items.ja: 食事：愛知県産ゆめまつり
items.section: 会席「蓬左」の献立 / Inside the ¥5,500 course
items.note: 食事 near the end of a kaiseki means rice, pickles and miso soup. ゆめまつり is a rice variety bred in Aichi. The rice itself is plain steamed white rice and is wheat-free and plant-based — the pickles and the miso alongside it are not necessarily either.

items.section: 会席「蓬左」の献立 / Inside the ¥5,500 course
items.note: Anmitsu is cubes of firm agar jelly with sweet azuki bean paste, fruit and black-sugar syrup poured over — cool, not very sweet, and the standard way a kaiseki finishes. Agar is seaweed and the beans are beans, so it is often accidentally suitable, but shiratama dumplings, gyūhi and the odd sponge topping vary by kitchen; ask.

items.ja: 八寸：月見豆腐　締め鯖寿司　兎百合根　烏賊黄身焼き　銀杏　零余子
items.romaji: Hassun: Tsukimi-dōfu, Shime-saba Zushi, Usagi Yurine, Ika Kimiyaki, Ginnan, Mukago
items.en: Assorted platter in the hitsumabushi set: moon tofu, vinegared mackerel sushi, lily bulb shaped as a rabbit, squid glazed with egg yolk, ginkgo nuts, yam bulbils
items.section: 一色産ひつまぶし和膳の献立 / Inside the hitsumabushi set
items.note: 八寸 is the seasonal showpiece platter, named for the eight-sun (24 cm) cedar tray it is served on, and it is where the kitchen shows off — here a rabbit carved from lily bulb and a moon of egg yolk, both autumn moon-viewing references. 銀杏 are ginkgo nuts, 零余子 the tiny bulbs that grow on yam vines. The 締め鯖 is cured in vinegar, and its sushi rice plus the glazes bring soy in.

items.ja: お抹茶　和三盆糖付
items.en: Whisked matcha with a wasanbon sugar sweet
items.section: カフェドリンク / Café drinks
items.note: Proper whisked matcha served with a piece of wasanbon — a fine-grained Japanese sugar pressed into a shape, eaten first so the sweetness cushions the tea's bitterness. Wasanbon is just sugarcane, but ask whether the sweet is plain pressed sugar or a wagashi with bean paste or gyūhi in it.

items.section: カフェドリンク / Café drinks
items.note: The house blend, with a decaf version on the same list — useful to know in a building where almost everything else is tea. Black coffee is wheat-free and plant-based; milk is the only thing to decline.

items.ja: 醸し人九平次 純米大吟醸／名古屋
items.en: Kuheiji junmai daiginjo sake, from Nagoya
items.section: 日本酒 / Sake
items.note: The city's most internationally known sake house — a Nagoya brewery that also farms rice in Hyōgo and makes wine in Burgundy, and the obvious local thing to drink here. Junmai daiginjo means rice, water and koji only, no added alcohol. Sake is made from rice, but brewers are not required to declare fining agents, so a strict celiac may still want to ask.

nagoya_shiboriyan_marunouchi.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Transcribed from the shop's own A-board and in-store menu card photographed 2026/03, weeks after it opened; the struck-through higher figures are the standard prices and the red ones are the lunch-time special.

items.en: Set meal A — one prawn fry, one piece of itoyori fry
items.section: 定食 / Set meals (lunch-time special price; normally ¥1,300)
items.note: The board lists exactly what is in each set. A gets you 海老フライ 1本 (one prawn), いとより 1枚 (one fillet of golden threadfin bream), 小鉢 (a small side), おしんこ (pickles), ご飯 (rice) and お味噌汁 (miso soup). Everything fried here is panko-crumbed, so wheat throughout; large rice is free at lunch.

items.en: Set meal B — two prawn fries
items.section: 定食 / Set meals (lunch-time special price; normally ¥1,500)
items.note: The pure ebi-fry option and the one to order if you came for Nagoya's signature fried prawn: 海老フライ 2本 plus small side, pickles, rice and miso soup. Panko is wheat and the tartare sauce it comes with is egg-based.

items.en: Set meal C — one prawn fry and two pieces of pork fillet katsu
items.section: 定食 / Set meals (lunch-time special price; normally ¥1,600)
items.note: The biggest set: 海老フライ 1本 plus ひれかつ 2枚 — hire-katsu is the lean tenderloin cut, drier and less rich than the fatty loin (rōsu) most tonkatsu shops use — with small side, pickles, rice and miso soup. Panko is wheat; if you want it Nagoya-style, this is what a miso-katsu tare would be poured over, but ask whether they serve one.

items.en: Set meal D — three pieces of itoyori fry
items.section: 定食 / Set meals (lunch-time special price; normally ¥1,300)
items.note: The all-fish set: いとより 3枚 with small side, pickles, rice and miso soup. This is the one that shows where the shop comes from — the family runs a ryokan on the coast at Minami-Chita, and the fish is the point rather than the pork. Panko is wheat.

items.section: 定食の内容 / What's in the sets
items.note: Nagoya's most-loved fried thing and the reason this shop exists: a big prawn straightened out, dipped in flour, egg and panko and deep-fried, served with tartare sauce and a lemon wedge. Flour and panko are both wheat.

items.en: Golden threadfin bream, crumbed and fried
items.section: 定食の内容 / What's in the sets
items.note: Itoyori-dai is a pink-skinned sea bream with a long thread trailing from its tail fin, prized for delicate white flesh that stays soft when fried. You will almost never see it on a fried-food menu outside a coastal shop — its presence here is the ryokan showing through. Panko is wheat.

items.section: 定食の内容 / What's in the sets
items.note: Hire is the tenderloin — the leanest cut, cut into thick medallions rather than one flat sheet, so it comes out juicy without the fat rim of a rōsu katsu. Wheat flour and panko.

items.en: Takeaway bento A — one prawn fry, one itoyori fry
items.section: お弁当 / Takeaway bento (special price; normally ¥1,300)
items.note: The bento board mirrors the set-meal board item for item, minus the miso soup, packed in a black tray with rice, salad and a tub of tartare. Same free large rice. Panko is wheat.

items.en: Takeaway bento B — two prawn fries
items.section: お弁当 / Takeaway bento (special price; normally ¥1,500)
items.note: Two whole panko prawns laid diagonally over the rice — the version to carry into Nagoya Castle park. Wheat.

items.en: Takeaway bento C — one prawn fry and two pork fillet katsu
items.section: お弁当 / Takeaway bento (special price; normally ¥1,650)
items.note: The mixed prawn-and-pork box, the most substantial of the four. Wheat.

items.en: Takeaway bento D — three itoyori fries
items.section: お弁当 / Takeaway bento (special price; normally ¥1,300)
items.note: All-fish box. Wheat.

items.ja: えびとかつ お弁当
items.section: お弁当 / Takeaway bento
items.note: The street sign advertises takeaway boxes from ¥800, below the four lettered bento — a cheaper entry box under the shop's own tagline, "prawn and katsu". Wheat throughout.

items.en: Free upgrade to a large rice
items.section: 定食 / Set meals
items.note: Printed in red across the top of both boards: the large rice costs nothing between 11:15 and 14:00, so say 大盛で (ōmori de) when you pay. Plain steamed white rice is the one wheat-free, plant-based thing in a shop that otherwise fries everything in panko — though it is scooped in that same kitchen. You pay at the register before sitting down; cash or PayPay only.

nagoya_brillance.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Course price from the restaurant's own (公式) listing, updated 2026/07/31; drink prices from its own drink list updated 2026/05/29. A 15% service charge is added. The individual plates below are one 2026 seating's line-up — the menu is a chef's omakase and rotates constantly.

items.section: コース / Course
items.note: There is one menu and this is it — a ten-course omakase, no à la carte. The restaurant is the Nagoya project of Shūzō Kishida of Tokyo's three-star Quintessence, with a head chef trained at Quintessence and at a two-star house in Paris. Reservation only, two people minimum, 16 and over, elegant-casual dress, 15% service on top. They ask for every diner's allergies and dislikes at booking and say they may not be able to accommodate anything raised on the day — so this is the rare high-end French kitchen where declaring coeliac in advance genuinely gets acted on.

items.ja: ヒラメ、赤満願寺、サブレ
items.section: コースの一例 / One seating's line-up
items.note: The opening bite. Manganji is a Kyoto heirloom sweet pepper, mild and thin-skinned, here in its red ripened form; the sablé is a savoury shortbread base. Sablé is butter and wheat flour.

items.section: コースの一例 / One seating's line-up
items.note: Chestnut velouté with slow-braised pork cheek — the cheek is worked muscle, so it goes gelatinous rather than dry. Velouté is classically thickened with a flour roux, though a chestnut soup often does not need one; ask.

items.ja: ヤギのミルクのババロア、百合根、マカダミアンナッツ、オリーブオイル
items.romaji: Yagi no Miruku no Babaroa, Yurine, Makadamian Nattsu, Oriibu Oiru
items.en: Goat's-milk bavarois, lily bulb, macadamia, olive oil
items.section: コースの一例 / One seating's line-up
items.note: A savoury bavarois — cream set with gelatine, here from goat's milk, so it carries the tang without the barnyard. 百合根 (yurine) is the edible bulb of a lily, scale by scale like a garlic head but sweet and floury when cooked; it is a Japanese ingredient French kitchens here love. Dairy and gelatine.

items.ja: 海老芋、イカスミ、アオリイカ
items.en: Shrimp taro, squid ink, bigfin reef squid
items.section: コースの一例 / One seating's line-up
items.note: 海老芋 is a taro variety curved and striped like a prawn, dense and sweet, a prestige winter vegetable in Japanese cooking. アオリイカ is bigfin reef squid — the sweetest and most expensive of the squids. Squid ink dishes sometimes carry a flour-thickened sauce; ask.

items.ja: 牛ランプ肉、生ハム、クルトン
items.section: コースの一例 / One seating's line-up
items.note: Rump is the cut just above the sirloin — lean, deeply beefy, and a deliberate choice over fattier wagyu cuts. Croutons are fried bread: wheat.

items.ja: フランス　ブルターニュオマール、ビスクソース
items.section: コースの一例 / One seating's line-up
items.note: Blue lobster from Brittany, the benchmark European lobster, with a sauce built from its own roasted shells. Classical bisque is thickened with rice or flour and finished with cognac — worth asking which.

items.ja: かも、めぐみがも、ゴボウ
items.section: コースの一例 / One seating's line-up
items.note: The main meat course. めぐみ鴨 is a named Japanese duck brand; ゴボウ is burdock, a long woody root with an earthy, almost smoky flavour that Japan eats as a vegetable and Europe mostly doesn't. Duck sauces are usually reduced stock and wine, but ask about flour and soy.

items.ja: マカロン、マスカルポーネ、安納芋
items.section: コースの一例 / One seating's line-up
items.note: 安納芋 is a sweet potato from Tanegashima so sugary and moist it eats like custard when baked. A true macaron is almond flour, egg white and sugar with no wheat, but pastry sections vary and share benches — ask rather than assume.

items.section: コースの一例 / One seating's line-up
items.note: The closing sweet. Meringue is egg white and sugar only, so the wheat question is whatever is under it. Dairy either way.

items.section: ドリンク / Drinks
items.note: From ¥22,000, poured by a sommelier across the ten courses; the printed note says the aperitif is charged separately. Wine is grape, but fining agents (egg white, isinglass, casein) are not declared on Japanese labels, so a strict vegan should ask.

items.section: ドリンク / Drinks
items.note: From ¥6,000 a glass. The bottle list behind it is one of the most serious in the city — over seventy champagnes from Egly-Ouriet and Selosse to Salon and a Krug Clos d'Ambonnay, and it is worth asking to see it even if you drink the pairing.

items.en: White or red wine by the glass
items.section: ドリンク / Drinks
items.note: From ¥4,200 a glass, either colour. Same fining caveat as the pairing.

items.section: オプション / Add-on
items.note: A hand-pulled sugar flower for a birthday or anniversary, ¥2,200 each, ordered by noon the day before; they will not write a name or message on it. Boiled sugar work is normally just sugar, glucose and colour.

nagoya_tantanmen_senmonten_meny.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Transcribed from the shop's own ticket machine photographed 2026/04 and its chalk A-board photographed 2026/06.

items.section: 担々麺 / Tantanmen
items.note: The shop's core bowl, advertised on the board as 濃厚胡麻が効いた — "thick with sesame". Japanese tantanmen is a soup noodle: a creamy sesame-paste-and-soy-milk broth over wheat noodles, topped with spicy minced pork and greens. Not the dry Sichuan original. Wheat noodles, wheat-soy seasoning, pork.

items.section: 担々麺 / Tantanmen
items.note: More noodles for ¥100. The machine offers three sizes on every bowl — 並 regular, 大 large, 特大 extra large — so pick the row, not just the column.

items.section: 担々麺 / Tantanmen
items.note: The top size, only ¥50 above large — the best value on the machine if you are hungry.

items.section: 担々麺 / Tantanmen
items.note: The board calls it 痺れる旨さ — "delicious numbness". 麻辣 (mala) is the Sichuan pairing of 麻 numbing Sichuan pepper and 辣 chilli heat; the tingling lip-buzz is the point, and it is a different sensation from plain spiciness. Large ¥1,200, extra large ¥1,250. Wheat noodles.

items.ja: チャーシュー担々麺　並
items.en: Tantanmen with extra braised pork, regular
items.section: 担々麺 / Tantanmen
items.note: The standard bowl loaded with the shop's own chāshū, which the A-board calls 高豚名物 — the house speciality. Large ¥1,300, extra large ¥1,350. Chāshū is braised in a soy-based liquid, so wheat twice over.

items.ja: チャーシュー麻辣担々麺　並
items.en: Mala tantanmen with extra braised pork, regular
items.section: 担々麺 / Tantanmen
items.note: The maximal bowl: numbing-spicy broth plus the full pork load. Large ¥1,400, extra large ¥1,450.

items.en: Brothless tantan mazesoba, with a rice chaser included
items.section: まぜそば / Mazesoba
items.note: The board bills it 胡麻と磯の融合 — sesame meets the sea, i.e. wakame was added to it. Mazesoba has no soup: thick noodles, a concentrated sauce and toppings at the bottom of the bowl that you stir hard yourself before eating. 追い飯 is the ritual finish — when the noodles are gone you tip the small bowl of rice into the leftover sauce and eat that too, and it is included in the price here. Wheat noodles.

items.section: トッピング / Toppings
items.note: Buy a separate ticket to step the chilli up. The default bowls are already properly spicy, so treat level 1 as a real increase rather than a nudge. Chilli oil bases sometimes carry soy or fermented bean paste; ask if it matters.

items.section: サイド / Sides
items.note: Boiled rather than pan-fried, so the wrapper stays slippery and soft — the northern-Chinese way and a much better match for a sesame broth than crisp gyoza. Wheat wrappers, pork filling.

items.en: Boiled dumplings with salt and aromatic chilli oil, six pieces
items.section: サイド / Sides
items.note: The A-board version — 塩と香味ラー油で食べる, eaten with salt and fragrant chilli oil instead of a vinegar-soy dip. ¥100 more than plain and the better order. Wheat wrappers.

items.ja: Aセット（水餃子4個＋ライス）
items.en: Set A — four boiled dumplings plus rice
items.section: セット / Sets
items.note: Three prices for three rice sizes: small ¥450, medium ¥500, large ¥550. Ordered alongside a bowl of noodles, not instead of one.

items.ja: Bセット（こく旨辣油水餃子4個＋ライス）
items.en: Set B — four chilli-oil dumplings plus rice
items.section: セット / Sets
items.note: Same idea as Set A with the rich chilli-oil dumplings: rice small ¥550, medium ¥600, large ¥650.

items.ja: Cセット（ミニチャーシュー丼）
items.en: Set C — mini braised-pork rice bowl
items.section: セット / Sets
items.note: A small bowl of rice under sliced chāshū, listed on the A-board at the same ¥450. The classic thing to order alongside a spicy bowl to cool it down. Soy-braised pork means wheat.

items.ja: ライス　小 / 中 / 大
items.section: サイド / Sides
items.note: Plain steamed white rice, unseasoned — the only wheat-free, plant-based thing on the machine, and useful either as a heat-quencher or as a substitute 追い飯 for the mazesoba. It is scooped in a kitchen full of wheat noodles, so it is survival food rather than a safe meal.

items.ja: 厚切りチャーシュー　1枚
items.section: トッピング / Toppings
items.note: A single thick slab rather than the usual paper-thin sheets — this is the cut the shop is named for (高豚 reads "Haiton", literally "high pork"). Soy-braised: wheat.

items.section: トッピング / Toppings
items.note: A whole plate of the chāshū as a dish in its own right — order it with a beer rather than on top of a bowl. Soy-braised: wheat.

items.section: トッピング / Toppings
items.note: A pile of shredded Japanese spring onion, flagged on the machine with a hand-written 大盛ネギ tag. Just the vegetable — no seasoning, no wheat.

items.ja: ちょい呑みビールセット
items.section: ドリンク / Drinks
items.note: Advertised on the street board: a beer plus a snack for ¥1,000, aimed at the Friday and Saturday late shift when the shop stays open to 22:00. Beer is malted barley.

items.ja: アサヒスーパードライ / サッポロ赤星
items.en: Asahi Super Dry / Sapporo Lager "Red Star"
items.section: ドリンク / Drinks
items.note: 赤星 is the old-fashioned Sapporo Lager in the red-star bottle — a heavier, maltier beer than Super Dry and the one older Japanese drinkers order on purpose. Barley: not gluten-free.

items.ja: サントリー角ハイボール / レモンチューハイ / ビンコーラ
items.romaji: Santorii Kaku Haibōru / Remon Chūhai / Bin Kōra
items.en: Suntory Kaku highball / lemon chūhai / bottled cola
items.section: ドリンク / Drinks
items.note: 角 is Suntory's yellow-labelled house whisky and the highball made from it is Japan's default drink with fried and spicy food. Chūhai is shōchū with soda and flavouring. Both are distilled, which removes gluten protein in practice, but coeliacs who react to grain spirits should stick to the cola.

nagoya_ramen_shima.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Transcribed from the shop's own printed menu sheet inside the shop (photographed 2026/03) and the identical weathered card by the door (photographed 2026/04); prices are marked 税込, tax included.

items.ja: しょうゆらーめん　並
items.section: らーめん / Ramen
items.note: The whole menu is this one bowl in four configurations. Old-school Nagoya shōyu ramen — a clear brown soy-seasoned broth, straight thin wheat noodles, a few slices of pork, menma and spring onion. ¥500 in 2026 is genuinely extraordinary and is why people cross town for it. Wheat noodles and wheat soy sauce; the broth is animal. Five counter seats, no ticket machine, cash only, smoking allowed; you order by saying the size — 並 (nami), 一人半 (ichininhan) or 大盛 (ōmori) — and whether you want チャーシュー.

items.ja: しょうゆらーめん　一人半
items.section: らーめん / Ramen
items.note: 一人半 literally means "one and a half people" — the middle size, between regular and large. An unusual old-shop way of writing it that you will rarely see elsewhere. Wheat.

items.ja: しょうゆらーめん　大盛
items.section: らーめん / Ramen
items.note: The biggest bowl, still under ¥1,000. Wheat.

items.en: Ramen loaded with braised pork — add ¥200 to any size
items.section: らーめん / Ramen
items.note: The card reads チャーシュー麺　各200円増 — the pork upgrade costs ¥200 on top of whichever size you pick, so ¥700 on a regular, ¥800 on the one-and-a-half, ¥900 on a large. Chāshū is simmered in soy: wheat.

items.section: 薬味 / Condiments
items.note: The card carries a separate note — ※にんにく有ります — that garlic is available; say にんにく入れてください to have it crushed into the bowl. No price shown, so it appears to be free. Plain garlic is just garlic.
